title: Decisions: The If Block
description: A sequence always does the same thing. A decision lets the robot's own path change based on what it actually finds.

content.value: Every decision has the same shape: check something, then choose one of two branches based on the answer. In flowcharts this is traditionally drawn as a diamond — one path in, two paths out, depending on true or false.

is there a wall ahead?
              /        \
           yes          no
            |            |
      (then branch)  (else branch)

You already met this exact idea back in Module 1: "if distance < 20, turn instead of driving forward" is a decision. Here, the block version checks a simpler question — is there a wall directly ahead — but it's structurally identical.

content.title: 🧩 Use if / else to navigate
content.hint: This maze has forks. Try an If wall ahead block: turn one way in the 'then' branch, keep going straight in the 'else' branch.

content.value: Notice what a decision buys you that a plain sequence can't: the same block program can now react differently depending on what's actually in front of the robot, instead of blindly following one fixed path. That's a real step toward the kind of autonomous behaviour this whole course has been building to.

An if block without an else isn't broken — it just means "do nothing extra" when the condition is false. Both branches existing side by side, though, is what makes a decision a true fork rather than an optional extra step.
Key takeaway: a decision checks a condition and runs one of two branches depending on the answer — the same shape as Module 1's "if distance < 20, turn," now something you build yourself.

quiz.question: What does an If block's 'then' branch run?
options: Only when the checked condition is true
Only when the checked condition is false
quiz.explain: The 'then' branch is specifically the true case — that's the whole point of branching on a condition.

quiz.question: What can a decision-using program do that a plain sequence-only program can't?
options: React differently depending on what it actually senses, instead of always following one fixed path
quiz.explain: That's the real power of a decision — the same program can produce different behaviour depending on the situation it's actually in.
